findings.title: Reintroduction of log injection via unsanitized geometry value
findings.description:
The code reverts to logging the raw user-supplied `value` directly into the error message. This reintroduces the log injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-111211) that the previous code explicitly addressed using `trim_value` and `log_message`. If an attacker submits a geometry value containing newline characters (e.g., `\n2026-01-01 INFO Admin logged in`), these control characters will be written unescaped into the log file, allowing log forgery and breaking log aggregation/parsing.

_SecurityAgent:_ The diff reverts a security fix (CVE-2026-111211) by removing the call to `trim_value` and `log_message`, which were designed to escape control characters and limit log size. The new code passes the raw, untrusted user input (`value`) directly to `logger.error`. This reintroduces a Log Injection vulnerability. An attacker can submit a malicious geometry string containing newline characters (`\n`), carriage returns (`\r`), or ANSI escape sequences (e.g., `\x1b[31m`). Since `value` is user-controlled and reaches the logger without sanitization, the attacker can forge log entries, manipulate log structure, or confuse log analysis tools. Additionally, without `trim_value`, an attacker can submit extremely large strings, causing potential log flooding or Denial of Service (DoS) via excessive disk I/O or log aggregation overhead. The removal of the corresponding unit tests (`test_deserialize_logs_escaped_value` and `test_deserialize_logs_trimmed_value`) confirms that this regression is not protected by the test suite.
findings.suggestion: Restore the use of `django.utils.log.log_message` and `django.utils.text.trim_value` to ensure values are properly escaped and trimmed before logging, or manually sanitize the `value` string to remove/escape control characters before passing it to the logger.
